prompt.context: Your client Fun Ventures, an established PE firm, is looking to acquire Nook Co., a hospitality group that specializes in developing and transforming uninhabited islands into premium and private vacation destinations. Nook Co. proposed an initial offer of $1.5 Billion. Fun Ventures would like your advice on whether they should proceed with the acquisition.
prompt.question: Should Fun Ventures proceed with the acquisition of Nook Co. at the proposed price of $1.5 Billion?

clarifying_info.q: What does Nook Co.'s business model look like?
clarifying_info.a: Nook Co. acquires ownership of islands, constructs resorts, and operates all on-island activities as well as transportation to and from the islands.
Nook Co. operates 10 islands across East Asia, with 5 additional islands in the construction pipeline. They serve customers internationally.

clarifying_info.q: What is Fun Ventures' timeline and return target?
clarifying_info.a: Fun Ventures is looking to make the decision as soon as possible and is targeting a 15% ROI.
There are four other global competitors; details will be provided later via exhibits.

exhibits.title: Nook Co. Resort Example (SE Asia Island)
exhibits.shows: A photo of a Nook Co. resort on an island in Southeast Asia, illustrating the type of premium vacation destination the company develops and operates.

exhibits.title: Island Resort Market Share 2015–2019
exhibits.shows: Stacked bar chart showing total market size (in USD) and each competitor's market share percentage from 2015 to 2019 for five players: Campfire Company, K.K. Vacation, Nook Co., DAL, and C.J. Limited.

exhibits.title: Competitors' Price and Gross Profit %
exhibits.shows: Scatter/bubble chart plotting each competitor's room rate per night (x-axis, in USD) against their profit margin % (y-axis) for Campfire Company, K.K. Vacation, DAL, and C.J. Limited.

data.note: Nook Co. is not shown; competitors range from ~$6,000 to ~$14,000 per night with profit margins roughly 15%–38%.

exhibits.title: Nook Co. Cost Structure
exhibits.shows: Table listing Nook Co.'s variable costs (COGS and salary) and fixed costs (SG&A) per cost category.

framework: Island Development Market: market size & growth, competitor landscape and market share, industry trends (rising affluent travelers, AI/tech usage)
Nook Co. Assessment: services offered (island development, travel, hospitality), customer profile (B2B/B2C, demographics), capabilities and assets (operations, distribution, HR)
Financial Analysis: valuation and valuation methods, ROI calculation vs. Fun Ventures' 15% target
Other Considerations: synergies with Fun Ventures' existing portfolio (travel agencies, construction), risks (legal/regulatory, environmental, financial manipulation)

questions.prompt: What is the potential market size for premium island vacations?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a top-down market sizing using world population, filtering to the ultra-high-net-worth segment, applying likelihood to visit, visit frequency, and average spend per stay. Key insight: market is approximately $1B/year.

math.setup: World population × % potential customers × % likelihood to visit ÷ visit frequency × spend per stay
steps: Visit frequency: once every 2 years → 80,000 / 2 = 40,000 stays/year
math.answer: Total market size ≈ $1 Billion per year

questions.prompt: What is the profit of Nook Co. in 2019?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 2 to read Nook Co.'s 2019 market share (~28%), apply it to the $1B market to get revenue, then use the headcount and Exhibit 4 cost structure to compute total costs. Key insights: (1) Nook Co. is the fastest-growing competitor; (2) it has high administrative costs that PE management could cut; (3) its ~30% profit margin is lower than leading competitors, suggesting it sacrificed margin to gain share.

math.setup: Revenue = market share × market size; Costs = variable costs (labor + food & supplies + transport) + fixed costs; Profit = Revenue − Costs

questions.prompt: Calculate the ROI on this acquisition and assess whether it meets Fun Ventures' target.
questions.guidance: Candidate should value Nook Co. using a perpetuity (NPV = annual profit / discount rate), then compute ROI = (NPV − purchase price) / NPV. Key insight: ROI of ~12% falls short of the 15% target. Excellent candidates will note that reducing the $30M administrative cost by ~$5M would push ROI above 15%, making the deal viable with PE-driven cost optimization.

math.setup: Perpetuity value = Annual profit / Discount rate; ROI = (NPV − Acquisition price) / NPV
steps: Sensitivity: if administrative costs cut by $5M → profit = $89M → NPV = $89M / 0.05 = $1.78B → ROI = ($1.78B − $1.5B) / $1.78B ≈ 15.7% > 15% target
math.answer: Base case ROI ≈ 12%, below the 15% target; cost reduction of ~$5M in admin costs would push ROI above 15%

brainstorming.prompt: What other potential risks would you like to consider in the acquisition of Nook Co.?

categories.name: Internal to Nook Co.
ideas: Unsustainable high growth rate (may not persist post-acquisition)
Customer churn if prices are raised to normal/market levels after acquisition
Generic service model with no clear competitive moat or differentiation
Risk of manipulated or overstated financial statements from Nook Co. management

categories.name: External / Macro
ideas: Global warming and rising sea levels could submerge or damage owned islands
Conflict of interest with other Fun Ventures portfolio companies (e.g., travel agencies, construction firms)
Shift in consumer preferences away from private island vacations
Safety, environmental, and legal regulations from government bodies restricting island development or operations

recommendation: If recommending YES: ROI is close to the 15% target and PE operational improvements (especially cutting ~$5M in administrative costs) can push it above threshold; Nook Co. also shows the fastest market share growth among all competitors and operates in a market with only four other players.

If recommending NO: The base-case ROI of ~12% does not meet Fun Ventures' 15% target; growth achieved partly through below-market pricing may be unsustainable long-term; profit margins are lower than leading competitors such as Campfire Company.
risks: Environmental risk: rising sea levels or natural disasters could impair owned island assets
Regulatory risk: government bodies may impose new restrictions on private island development
Financial integrity risk: Nook Co. financials may not be fully reliable; due diligence required
Market risk: rapid growth may slow or reverse if pricing is normalized post-acquisition
next_steps: Form a taskforce to conduct full due diligence on Nook Co.'s balance sheet and verify financial statements
Commission market research on the current customer base to forecast sustainable growth and gauge price sensitivity
Identify specific cost reduction levers (especially the $30M administrative cost line) that Fun Ventures' management team can execute post-close
Evaluate synergies with existing Fun Ventures portfolio companies (travel agencies, construction)
